extracted.intended_audience: SBIR/STTR program managers at federal agencies, SBA staff, and small businesses applying for SBIR/STTR awards
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and reporting standards for administering, reporting, and evaluating federal SBIR and STTR programs across participating agencies, and for small businesses applying for or receiving awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR/STTR mission and program goals
rubrics_metrics.description: The goals of the SBIR and STTR programs are to: Stimulate technological innovation; Use small businesses to meet Federal Government R/R&D needs; Foster and encourage participation in innovation and entrepreneurship by women and socially and economically disadvantaged individuals; Increase private-sector commercialization of innovations derived from federal R/R&D funding; Stimulate a partnership of ideas and technologies between innovative small businesses and non-profit Research Institutions (STTR only).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These stated goals serve as high-level criteria for program design, solicitation topics, outreach, and evaluation of program success (e.g., commercialization outcomes and diverse participation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Participating Agencies and applicability thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal agencies with extramural R/R&D budgets exceeding $100 million were required to obligate a minimum of 3.2% of the FY22 extramural R/R&D budget for SBIR awards; agencies with extramural R/R&D budgets exceeding $1 billion were required to obligate a minimum of 0.45% for STTR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies meeting the budget thresholds are subject to SBIR/STTR minimum spending requirements as mandated by the Small Business Act; SBA assesses compliance with these percentages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of extramural budget
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 9(e)(1) defines extramural budget as: '[T]he sum of the total obligations minus amounts obligated for such activities by employees of the agency in or through government-owned, government-operated facilities,' with specified exceptions for DOE and USAID.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this statutory definition (and cited exceptions) when calculating the base for minimum spending requirement percentages; SBA compares agency-provided extramural R/R&D to NCSES/NSF reported figures during validation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program structure — Three phases
rubrics_metrics.description: SBIR/STTR Programs are structured in three phases: Phase I (feasibility-related experimental study or theoretical R/R&D), Phase II (continued R/R&D effort), Phase III (commercialization effort).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solicitations, awards, and reporting should align activities and expectations to the appropriate phase definition; agencies may design solicitations and evaluation criteria consistent with phase purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase I purpose, amounts, and period
rubrics_metrics.description: The purpose of Phase I is to determine the scientific and technical merit, feasibility, and commercial potential of the proposed R/R&D efforts and to determine the quality of performance of the small business awardee prior to providing further federal support in Phase II. SBIR/STTR Phase I awards generally range from $100,000 to $275,000 for a 6 to 12-month period of performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phase I proposals and evaluations should focus on feasibility, merit, and commercial potential; award decisions and scope should reflect typical funding and duration ranges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase II purpose, amounts, and period
rubrics_metrics.description: The objective of Phase II is to continue the R/R&D efforts initiated in Phase I. Funding is based on the results achieved in Phase I and the scientific and technical merit and commercial potential of the project proposed in Phase II. SBIR/STTR Phase II awards generally range from $750,000 to $1,838,000 for a two-year period of performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phase II selection should prioritize demonstrated Phase I results, technical merit, and commercialization potential; agencies may award Sequential Phase IIs per 15 U.S.C. § 638(ff) and other authorized continuation/assistance mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase III definition and procurement preference
rubrics_metrics.description: Phase III refers to work that derives from, extends, or completes an effort made through a SBIR/STTR-funded Phase I or II R/R&D but is funded by sources other than the SBIR/STTR Programs. To the greatest extent practicable, federal entities, including government prime contractors, pursuing products, production, services, or R/R&D developed under the SBIR/STTR Programs shall issue Phase III awards to the SBIR/STTR awardee that developed the technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because initial Phase I/II competition satisfies procurement competition requirements, agencies may issue direct or sole-source Phase III awards to the original awardee where practicable; agencies should track and report Government Phase III funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR.gov data and submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Participating Agencies are required to provide solicitations, applicant proposal data, award information, annual report submissions, and commercialization data through SBIR.gov per SBIR Policy Directive (§5(e)(2), §10(e), §10(f), §10(h), §10(g)). Agencies must post solicitations to SBIR.gov within five business days of the solicitation open date and upload annual report data by March 15.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely and complete uploads (solicitations, applications, awards, commercialization info, and annual report) are mandatory; SBA monitors submission timeliness and completeness and lists submission dates and 'early/on-time/late' status.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBA's compliance determination process
rubrics_metrics.description: SBA determines whether an agency meets the minimum spending requirements established in sections 9(f) and (n) of the Small Business Act by compiling and evaluating data across agencies and comparing agency-provided extramural R/R&D obligations to NCSES/NSF reported figures; SBA's analysis of agency compliance is described in Section 7.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should provide accurate data to SBIR.gov and anticipate SBA validation; an agency may appear 'Complied' based on agency data but 'Did Not Comply' after SBA assessment against NSF NCSES data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection rate reporting caveat
rubrics_metrics.description: The selection rate is an estimate. For FY22 awards, the proposals received were from both FY21 and FY22.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting selection rates, note cross-fiscal-year proposal intake may make simple ratios approximate; agencies should annotate selection rates accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required reporting metrics and tables
rubrics_metrics.description: The annual report measures multiple factors including obligations by agency, socioeconomic participation (WOSB, SDB, HUBZone), selection rates, award timelines (time between solicitation close and award notification; time between Phase I award end and Phase II start), awards exceeding guideline amounts, awards by state/territory, Administrative Funding Pilot and commercialization program metrics, and Government Phase III funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must supply the data fields used to populate these tables/charts to enable consistent cross-agency comparison; SBA aggregates and analyzes these metrics in specified tables and charts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Socioeconomic participation mandates and definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Congress directs the SBIR Program to foster and encourage participation by women-owned small businesses (WOSB), socially and economically disadvantaged small businesses (SDB), and HUBZone firms; definitions for WOSB, SDB, and HUBZone are found in the Policy Directive (§3(ss), §3(ll)) and 15 U.S.C. §632(p)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should collect and report award and proposal data by these socioeconomic groups and align outreach and solicitation strategies to promote participation from these populations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical and Business Assistance (TABA) reporting and use
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical and Business Assistance (TABA) Provided by Agency ($) and TABA Provided to Small Businesses in Award Obligations ($) are reported. These are TABA funds provided by the agency directly to the awardee through grant or contract and thus already included in PI/PII obligation award amounts (with exceptions noted, e.g., DOT).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must report TABA funding and indicate whether amounts are included in reported Phase I/II obligations; DOT TABA is an exception and must be reported separately as noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative Funding Pilot Program (AFPP) rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative Funding Pilot (AFPP) (3%) ($) is a line item in agency reporting (AFPP at 3% shown in tables).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies piloting administrative funding should track AFPP expenditures and report amounts as specified in annual report tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercialization emphasis in proposal evaluation (EPA example)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA states that the proposal evaluation criteria emphasize commercialization, including a focus on intellectual property, market opportunity and the business expertise of the team. External reviewers with commercialization experience review all Phase I and Phase II proposals and provide evaluations which impact final funding decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies aiming to emphasize commercialization should include commercialization criteria in proposal evaluations and use reviewers with commercialization expertise; provide commercialization assistance and options (e.g., EPA's up to $100,000 supplement for securing 3rd-party investment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicitation topic development and alignment with agency mission
rubrics_metrics.description: Participating agencies designate R/R&D topics in solicitations that address agency missions and needs; NASA notes subtopic descriptions were developed by NASA’s technical experts and aligned to Agency mission directorates and center needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solicitations and subtopics should be crafted by technical experts to reflect agency mission needs; topic design influences selection and later Phase III infusion into agency missions (e.g., NASA sequential Phase IIs targeted to Artemis).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of awards and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies are expected to meet timelines (e.g., solicitations posted within five business days; annual report by March 15; EPA made 100% of new awards within the required timelines through streamlined review and online review platform).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should implement processes and platforms to meet statutory/regulatory timelines and report performance; timely award notifications and uploads are tracked in the annual report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of competition status to enable Phase III sole-source awards
rubrics_metrics.description: The competition for SBIR/STTR Phase I and Phase II awards satisfies competition requirements, allowing federal agencies to issue direct or sole-source awards to SBIR/STTR awardees for Phase III efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should document Phase I/II competition as the basis for any direct/sole-source Phase III actions and track government Phase III obligations to SBIR/STTR awardees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting of awards exceeding guideline amounts
rubrics_metrics.description: The report includes monitoring of 'Awards Exceeding Guideline Amounts' and specifically lists awards exceeding guideline amounts by more than 50% (Table 18).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must report awards that exceed standard guideline amounts and provide details; SBA aggregates and reports such instances for oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data integrity, submission, and validation best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: SBA focused on solutions to ensure agencies could upload and verify data in an accurate and cost-effective manner; SBA validates agency submissions (comparing agency data to NSF NCSES) and documents discrepancies (Section 7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should adopt data integrity and submission best practices (timely uploads, verification, reconciliation with NCSES) to reduce variance and ensure accurate compliance determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercialization and outreach programs reporting (CRPP, CCRPP, I-Corps, CAM, TABA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies report on commercialization readiness/assistance programs (Commercialization Readiness Pilot Program (CRPP), Civilian Commercialization Readiness Pilot Program (CCRPP), I-Corps participation, Commercialization Assistance Marketplace (CAM), TABA, and similar outreach activities) and their funding/results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs that support translation to market should be tracked (participants, follow-on investments, matched funding, Phase III outcomes) and reported as part of agency commercialization metrics.
